__NOTOC__

This page is the interface between Emma (human) and the bot agents that work on this wiki. Agents post open questions and blockers here when they hit a decision that requires human judgement. Emma answers them on the wiki. Agents read the wiki version each session and act on the answers.

== How to use this page ==

* '''Agents:''' read this page at the start of every session AND every hourly work-loop cron tick. When you hit a blocker (a design call, a credential need, a wiki-side action you cannot take, an ambiguous instruction), add it under the relevant section below with enough context that Emma can answer without re-deriving the problem. Don't move items out of "blocked" sections on your own — wait for Emma's edit on the wiki. '''When you verify an item has actually been resolved (via code/API/log inspection), delete the bullet entirely in the same commit''' — leaving stale "open questions" lying around is a failure mode Emma has flagged. Investigate before declaring something blocked-on-Emma; many items framed as blockers are either already resolved or are autonomous work that just needs to be started.
* '''Emma:''' edit answers in-line under each question. When you've answered a question and the agents have acted on it, strike or delete the question. Free-form notes that don't fit anywhere else go under [[#Notes|Notes]] below.
* '''This page is different from other git-synced pages.''' The wiki is the canonical source of truth here. When Emma edits this page on shinto.miraheze.org, those edits propagate down to the repo (wiki-wins for this page). Agents must not silently overwrite Emma's wiki edits with stale repo content.

== Sync-policy exception note ==

Files in <code>git_synced/</code> use revision-aware conflict resolution as of 2026-05-27 (whichever side is further ahead in revisions wins; static repo-wins is the tie-break fallback). This page is intended to be edited primarily ON the wiki by Emma, and her edits should accumulate revisions faster than agent-side edits, so the revision-aware policy should naturally favour wiki content. Agents working on <code>shintowiki-scripts</code> should additionally:

# Always pull this page from the wiki at the start of a session (don't trust the repo copy alone).
# When committing changes to other files, never include a stale repo version of this page in a sync push.
# If you're about to edit this file in the repo, first confirm the wiki version hasn't been updated since the last sync — otherwise you'd risk clobbering Emma's answers.
